sec: Variceal bleeds: determinants and natural history · p1004

items.q: The main factor in variceal bleeds, as stated on p1004, is:
items.exp: Determinants: main factor — variceal wall tension. (Book p1004)

items.q: Match the p1004 determinants of variceal bleeding — 1) Main factor  2) Vessel component  3) Pressure component  4) The bracketed note on diameter + pressure … A) Pressure  B) Variceal wall tension  C) Vessel diameter  D) Directly related to HVPG
items.exp: Main factor: variceal wall tension; determined by vessel diameter + pressure; bracket: directly related to HVPG. (Book p1004)

items.q: The p1004 line ‘Gastric esophageal varices : 50% cause cirrhosis’ attributes varices to cirrhosis in what proportion (as printed)?
items.exp: Causes: gastric esophageal varices : 50% cause cirrhosis (as printed). (Book p1004)

items.q: The development rate of varices in patients without varices, per p1004, is:
items.exp: Causes: without varices development rate : 8% per year. (Book p1004)

items.q: The variceal hemorrhage occurrence rate given on p1004 is:
items.exp: Causes: variceal hemorrhage occurrence rate : 5–15% per year. (Book p1004)

items.q: Match the p1004 risk-of-bleeding figures with the varix size — 1) Small varices (≤ 5 mm)  2) Large varices … A) 30%/year  B) < 10%/year
items.exp: Risk of bleeding: small varices (≤ 5 mm) : < 10%/year; large varices : 30%/year. (Book p1004)

items.q: Mortality from variceal bleeding, as printed on p1004, is:
items.exp: Causes: mortality from variceal bleeding : 15–30%. (Book p1004)

items.q: A cirrhotic is found to have large oesophageal varices on screening. Using only the p1004 figures, the pair that describes his annual bleed risk and the case-fatality if a bleed occurs is:
items.exp: Large varices : 30%/year risk; mortality from variceal bleeding : 15–30%. (Book p1004)
